sermon.title: When the Field Won’t Respond Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “When the Field Won’t Respond Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Ezekiel 2 on what a Christian is to do when immoral, sinning believers will not listen: do not be afraid of them, do not be dismayed by their looks, speak God’s words rather than your opinions, and take in the judgment Scriptures along with the encouraging ones. He gives examples from a protest he attended, urges Bible studies that ask what God is saying, and says ministers, politicians and church members bend Scripture to keep votes, members and benefits.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Statistics and claims about named people, groups and events are the speaker’s own and have not been checked by this site. Where he reads Scripture aloud his wording often differs slightly from the NKJV text shown with each section.

Okay, number one, they are a rebellious nation. They are disrespectful. They are stubborn. Wow, sound like anybody you know? “I send you to them, saying, ‘Thus saith the Lord.’ Whether they hear or whether they refuse to hear, they are a rebellious house.” Okay, so He’s sending, He’s describing God’s people in captivity being punished for their sins, and they’re still rebellious. He’s given a commandment, He’s given a charge, He’s given a mission to speak to them anyway, whether they listen or whether they don’t.

chunks.section_question: What did he tell the cameras about breaking a moral law?
chunks.short_answer: He says he told the newscasters that when we break a moral law it is a crime, that homosexuality is immoral, and that in his view such people “should be punished for it, disciplined for it, fined or something, not put on display for everybody to imitate.” He adds that the news did not repeat what he said. This is the speaker’s own strongly stated opinion.

The news just uses what’s good for them, what they like. Hallelujah. I told them that homosexuality is criminal, it’s a crime. And the newscasters, the camera people, they came up and said, “What do you mean by that?” I said, “When we break a moral law, it is a crime, and homosexuality is immoral, and they should be punished for it, disciplined for it, fined or something, not put on display for everybody to imitate.” Right? We don’t put the pedophiles on display. We don’t put incest people on display. Why are we letting these homosexuals get on TV and public places and everything like it’s normal and not a crime? It is a crime. Amen. See, we got to preach the word of the Lord. And yeah, they didn’t like it, and yeah, they got mad at me, and yeah, they attacked me at the beginning, till the leader got them in control. And I know why they did it, ’cause they attack me all the time. But when that camera comes, they are the nicest, most mannered people you can’t believe, because they don’t want the real attitude coming out.

chunks.section_question: Should we speak God’s words or our own opinions?
chunks.short_answer: He says to speak God’s words, “not your opinions, not what you believe.” He says God cares that you believe what He believes, and that we must change our thinking when it doesn’t line up with His.
chunks.text: Hallelujah. Speak My words, not your opinions, not what you believe. God doesn’t care what you believe; He cares that you believe what He believes. And we got to change our belief, and we got to change our thinking when it doesn’t line up with His. “Whether they hear, whether they refuse, for they are a rebellious house. But you, son of man, hear what I say to you. Do not be rebellious like the rebellious house.” Don’t follow their ways. Don’t accept their speech. Don’t accept their behavior. Don’t follow their ways. faqs.question: What is “When the Field Won’t Respond Part 1” about?
faqs.answer: He asks what a Christian is to do when the harvest field is unresponsive, and begins with immoral believers who will not listen, using Ezekiel 2.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And He said to me: “Son of man, I am sending you to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me; they and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day. For they are impudent and stubborn children. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD.’ As for them, whether they hear or whether they refuse—for they are a rebellious house—yet they will know that a prophet has been among them.

faqs.question: Who was Ezekiel sent to?
faqs.answer: He says Ezekiel was sent to the Jews in captivity who were being corrected for their sins and were still rebellious, disrespectful and stubborn.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And He said to me: “Son of man, I am sending you to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me; they and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day. For they are impudent and stubborn children. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD.’ As for them, whether they hear or whether they refuse—for they are a rebellious house—yet they will know that a prophet has been among them.

faqs.question: What if they won’t listen anyway?
faqs.answer: He says Ezekiel was given a charge to speak to them anyway, whether they listened or not, and that they would know a prophet had been among them.

faqs.question: What are the requirements for speaking to a hard harvest field of sinning believers?
faqs.answer: From Ezekiel 2 he lists: do not be afraid of them, do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their looks, and speak God’s words. He later adds eating the scroll, which carries the judgment Scriptures.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them nor be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are with you and you dwell among scorpions; do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their looks, though they are a rebellious house. You shall speak My words to them, whether they hear or whether they refuse, for they are rebellious. But you, son of man, hear what I say to you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house; open your mouth and eat what I give you.”

Now when I looked, there was a hand stretched out to me; and behold, a scroll of a book was in it. Then He spread it before me; and there was writing on the inside and on the outside, and written on it were lamentations and mourning and woe.

faqs.question: What replaces fear in a Christian walk?
faqs.answer: He says “courage replaces fear,” so that you do not even think about retaliation or offending.

faqs.question: Does God care what we believe?
faqs.answer: He says God doesn’t care what you believe; He cares that you believe what He believes, and we must change our thinking when it doesn’t line up with His.

faqs.question: Why does he say many Christians don’t know the word of God?
faqs.answer: He says they don’t get into the Bible and seek God, and let famous authors and pastors tell them what God is saying, and so they speak opinions and beliefs instead of the word of God.

faqs.question: Is there more than one way into the kingdom?
faqs.answer: He says there is no way into the kingdom but one, and that is through Christ. You cannot bend the scriptures to get someone accepted.

faqs.question: Does “God is love” mean He doesn’t correct us?
faqs.answer: He says God is love, and the Bible says a father who loves his child will discipline and correct him to spare him from death and destruction, and the spiritual Father does the same with us.

faqs.question: What does it mean to “eat the scroll” in Ezekiel 2?
faqs.answer: He says the scroll was written on both sides with the judgmental scriptures of lamentations, mourning and woe, not with “positive scriptures,” because there is a judgment of God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now when I looked, there was a hand stretched out to me; and behold, a scroll of a book was in it. Then He spread it before me; and there was writing on the inside and on the outside, and written on it were lamentations and mourning and woe.

faqs.question: Did Jesus preach about eternal punishment?
faqs.answer: He says yes, and points to Jesus telling a man to go and sin no more lest something worse come upon him: God will correct you now, and if you don’t turn around, He will correct you for eternity.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Afterward Jesus found him in the temple, and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Sin no more, lest a worse thing come upon you.”

faqs.question: What does he say 1 Corinthians 11 means about the weak, sick and those who die early?
faqs.answer: He calls it a judgment scripture to believers who are weak, sick and die before their time because they do not learn and recognize the body of the Lord Jesus Christ, which is His church.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy manner eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body. For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep.

faqs.question: What does he say is the focus and goal of God?
faqs.answer: He says the focus and goal of God is that you live right and speak right, bridle your tongue and bridle your body. When you make mistakes, you repent, get up and keep going.

faqs.question: What did the people say to Isaiah?
faqs.answer: He says they told Isaiah, “Do not prophesy to us right things, but speak to us smooth things, flattery,” and to prophesy deceits.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Who say to the seers, “Do not see,” And to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us right things; Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits.

faqs.question: What does he say happened to Paul and Peter when they spoke truth?
faqs.answer: He says they were beaten, stoned and put in prison because they spoke truth, and that if you speak truth, you will get people disliking you.
